standard.title: Geosynthetics — Geogrids for Flexible Pavements — Specification
standard.description: This standard specifies the quality, raw material, and performance requirements for polymeric geogrids (including uniaxial and biaxial geogrids) used for reinforcement, stabilization, and stress-distribution layers in flexible pavement structures. These geogrids are placed between pavement layers (such as weak subgrades, sub-base, or bituminous courses) in expressways, highways, runways, and rural roads to increase load-bearing capacity, reduce rutting, and minimize structural deformation.

amendments.summary: Inserts Clause 3.9 'Style Number' to establish a standard theoretical designation code representing the geogrid's designed ultimate tensile strength in the machine direction (MD) and cross-machine direction (CD) (e.g., style number '30/40' designates an ultimate tensile strength of 30 kN/m in the MD and 40 kN/m in the CD).

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Geo Textiles (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all geogrids for flexible pavements manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, stocking, selling, or importing non-certified geogrids is a legal offence. Export-only products conform to buyer specifications but are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic polymers and technical textiles.
requirements: Every roll of geogrid conforming to this standard must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) permanently printed or tagged, detailing the manufacturer's licence number (CM/L).
Each geogrid roll must be marked with a designated style number detailing its MD and CD ultimate tensile strengths (e.g. '20/20', '30/30', '40/40', '50/50', '30/40', etc.).

Geogrids must be manufactured from high-durability polymer resins (including polypropylene PP, high-density polyethylene HDPE, or high-tenacity polyester PET multifilament yarns). For PET-based geogrids, the raw yarns must satisfy strict molecular parameters: high molecular weight (> 25000 g/mol) and a low carboxyl end group (CEG) count (< 30 mmol/kg) to provide superior resistance to hydrolytic creep over a design life of up to 120 years.

Ultimate tensile strength (MD and CD) must comply with the designated style numbers, verified via wide-width tensile tests under IS 16635. Standard biaxial reinforcement strengths range from 20 kN/m up to 150 kN/m or more.

Geogrid rib junctions must undergo a mandatory pull-off test as specified in Annex B to evaluate junction strength (matching designed style strengths, e.g., 20/20, 30/30, 40/40). High junction efficiency is required to ensure consistent stress transfer across the interlocking aggregate-soil matrix.

Polyolefin-based geogrids must incorporate a uniform carbon black addition (typically 2.0% to 3.0%) for UV light stabilization. After undergoing 500 hours of continuous Xenon-arc UV weathering (per IS 13162 Part 2), the geogrid must retain at least 70% to 80% of its original ultimate tensile strength.

Knitted or woven polyester (PET) geogrids must be encased in a robust polymeric (e.g., PVC or acrylic) coating. The coating must provide a high barrier to mechanical installation damage, biological attack, and aggressive soil chemical environments.
Aperture sizes (typically 20 mm to 40 mm) must be sized appropriately to ensure mechanical aggregate interlock (the 'snowshoe effect') without allowing granular base leaching.
